items.reason: AC 'At /?brand={id} title reads Brand: {name} and subtitle holds All brands' fails, and AC 'unknown brand id keeps Ready for a new adventure?' fails: the header is blank. Because brandLookupPending is true on the first render, neither SectionContent block is rendered, so the SectionOutlet has no content component in the DOM and the later streamed SectionContent update is never applied.
items.fix: Render both SectionContent blocks on every render and vary only their content (for example, empty title while pending, then 'Brand: {name}' or the usual title and subtitle), or drop the pending state so content exists at the first flush. Then re-check /?brand=1, /?brand=999 and the card click in the browser.

items.reason: AC 'A linked card looks like the unlinked card ... and keeps a visible focus style' fails: `.brand-card-link .brand-card { height: 100% }` on a content-box article makes linked cards 44px taller than unlinked ones, removes the grid row gap, overlaps the next row, and leaves the focus outline misaligned with the card.
items.fix: Remove the height:100% rule (the <a> already stretches in the grid), or give the article box-sizing: border-box, so linked and unlinked cards are the same size and the focus ring traces the card.

items.reason: The new header lookup adds an API request on every single-brand catalog load. This violates the explicit 'No new API call' acceptance criterion; no ticket line authorizes the duplicate request.
items.fix: Share the existing GetBrands() result between the catalog header and filter component so each page load fetches brands once, keeping CatalogService and ICatalogService unchanged.

items.title: Selecting a brand's card opens the catalog filtered to that brand
covers: AC1: selecting a brand's card opens the catalog filtered to that brand
items.reason: AC1 is the core of the story. If the card is not a link, or links to the unfiltered catalog, the shopper never reaches the brand's products. e2e because the link lives on a Blazor page and the filter is applied by the catalog page from the URL.

items.title: The card applies the same filter as choosing the brand in the catalog's Brand filter
covers: AC1: the same filter as choosing the brand in the catalog's Brand filter
items.reason: AC1 says the card's result is "the same filter as choosing the brand in the catalog's Brand filter". A card that used another query parameter or another page would look filtered while differing from the filter (different count, filter tag not active, different URL to share). Comparing the two journeys guards that equivalence. e2e because both journeys are browser navigation.

items.title: Every brand card with products links to the catalog filtered to its own brand
covers: AC1: a brand's card (every brand with products)
items.reason: AC1 applies to any brand's card. A loop that links every card to the same id, or an off-by-one between card and brand, would pass TC-BRAND-2-01 for one brand and fail shoppers for the others. Checking all 13 demo cards' targets catches that without clicking each one. e2e because the hrefs are rendered by the Brands page.

items.title: Catalog filtered to one brand shows "Brand: Daybird" instead of the usual title
covers: AC2: header title "Brand: <name>" instead of the usual title
items.reason: AC2 makes the header tell the shopper which brand they are looking at, with the ticket's own example "Brand: Daybird". The risk is a title that keeps the usual text, shows the id instead of the name, or shows both. e2e because the title is a section rendered into the layout's header by the streamed catalog page.

items.title: "All brands" link under the brand title opens the Brands page
covers: AC2: "All brands" link under the title opens the Brands page
items.reason: AC2 gives the shopper a way back to the other brands. The link must sit under the title (the header subtitle) and lead to the Brands page; a link to `/` (the unfiltered catalog) would look right and break the story's "go back to the other brands". e2e because it is a navigation through the header.

items.title: Choosing one brand in the catalog's Brand filter also names it in the header
covers: AC2: any catalog filtered to exactly one brand, reached through the Brand filter
items.reason: AC2's precondition is "the catalog is filtered to exactly one brand", not "came from a brand card". A header that only changes when the shopper arrives from the Brands page would break the rule for shoppers who use the filter. Gravitator is used so the name is not hard-coded from the Daybird cases. e2e because the filter is a navigation inside the catalog page.

items.title: One brand plus a type filter still names the brand in the header
covers: AC2: exactly one brand selected, together with a type filter
items.reason: AC2 and AC3 depend only on how many brands are selected. A check written as "the query has exactly one filter value" would drop the brand title as soon as the shopper also picks a type. e2e because the combination is a catalog URL rendered by the WebApp.

items.title: Catalog without a brand filter shows the usual title and no "All brands" link
covers: AC3: no brand filter shows the usual title and no "All brands" link
items.reason: AC3 keeps the existing header for the plain catalog. A change that always renders a brand section, or leaves the title empty when no brand is selected, would break the catalog's landing page. e2e because the header is rendered on the test stack's home page.

items.title: Catalog filtered to two brands shows the usual title and no "All brands" link
covers: AC3: more than one brand selected shows the usual title and no "All brands" link
Implementation Notes: two brand query values
items.reason: AC3 is the boundary of AC2: one brand gets the brand title, two do not. Naming only the first brand, or "Brand: Daybird, Gravitator", would mislabel the page. The Implementation Notes ask for two `brand` query values. e2e because the header is rendered from the catalog URL on the test stack.

items.title: Card of a brand without products is not a link and says "No products yet"
covers: AC4: card without products is not a link
items.reason: AC4 keeps a brand without products from leading to an empty catalog page, and keeps BRAND-1's "No products yet" text. Wrapping every card in a link would break the first; reworking the card for the link would risk the second. The demo catalog has no brand without products, so scenario `brand-1` provides "Acme Empty". e2e because both outcomes are rendered markup and click behaviour on the Brands page.
